title: How to trigger an event (player transfer) by pressing enter / mouse click like a PPT

posts.author: CicakMemasak
posts.body:
I have a tutorial with just image that I set as a parallax background for the map. The idea is the tutorial goes on like a power point. However somehow I can't trigger the action to go to the next map when I press enter , space bar, and even mouse click.
Is there a plug in for that? Or did I set it up wrong?
I tried to use Auto Run and it just became automatic, which I don't want.
Sorry if this is a silly question!!

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
I think creating entirely separate maps for each image is a bit overkill.
Why don't you just use the "Show Picture" Command, and using a blank text box to pause between each picture?

posts.body:

-----------
Your event isn't working because you have the Trigger set to Action Button. This means the player needs to specifically interact with the event's hitbox.
Enter and Spacebar don't do anything in RPG Maker MV by default. You would have to create a plugin that changes your game's input code so that "Enter and Spacebar = a command the game understands" to make those buttons do anything. I won't get into that here, but you can find threads about it if you want to change your game's accepted input.
If you want the player to transfer maps when they press a button, from anywhere on the map ->
An easy way with no plugins required is to create a parallel event on the map with a looping command that checks for player input, and then transfers the player to a new map.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
While it's appreciated that
@Niniann
clarified some points about RPG Maker's internal logic, I want to make further clarifications with the provided suggestion:
While this does accomplish your original intent of transferring maps for each picture, this does not address the fact that it's a very inefficient way of just showing pictures. The reason why you don't want to do this is:
A minor concern are the map limitations. You can only have so many maps in a single RPG Maker project. While it's a rather high number, it's still unnecessary to eat into that limit when it's not necessary.
A larger concern is going to be project organization. It will become difficult to organize things when your map tree becomes a mess due to devoting entire maps to pictures.
This is why I proposed the blank message box and show picture command. It is simple and elegant and accomplishes exactly what you are attempting to do while being capable of being ran on any map at any time.
The second concern with Niniann's recommendation is the use of parallels to track input.
To make this clear; there is nothing inherently wrong with using parallel events.
However, since you are new to RPG Maker, it's good to learn some of the basic functions before you start overly relying on less efficient methods to handle things. Once you understand foundational stuff, you can build on it and better utilize parallel events.
The other concern with the designed parallel event Niniann proposed is that, in order to check player input, you would ideally want it to check as frequently as possible for input, and at 10 wait frames, this is going to make the event feel unresponsive. This might result in players pressing OK but the input not being registered.
If you go about this method I recommend using 3 wait frames or less.
To make this clear: the low wait frame time is just for checking input.
When using parallels to update other info, having slower wait times is better (such as 10 frames). But that's outside the scope of this post.
I once again recommend using show picture commands + a blank text box.
